summary:
Landing humans on Mars fails if astronauts set up their habitat or mobile workstation in the wrong location. Flat plains ideal for safe landings often lack accessible water ice, while ice-rich mid-latitude regions frequently suffer from steep slopes, radiation exposure, and seasonal dust storms that choke solar power. Mission planners and astronauts need a fast, unified decision-support tool that turns raw planetary science data into immediate survival decisions.

we intentionally engineered ARES-LOCATE to be ultra-lightweight—running in under 100 kilobytes on low-power hardware—because astronauts on Mars won't have a cloud data center next to their habitat. Today, our browser engine fuses NASA MOLA, SHARAD, and THEMIS metrics to locate safe, ice-rich workstations and simulate dust storm survival in milliseconds. When connected to full-scale NASA HiRISE LiDAR pipelines and live orbital weather telemetry, this exact architecture scales into an autonomous mission-control co-pilot for the first human Mars landing.. also for whole 3d mars we didnt had true resources and power..
details:
ARES-LOCATE is an ultra-lightweight Martian mission co-pilot that helps astronauts and mission planners find the safest places to build a base on Mars. Using real NASA datasets (MOLA elevation, MRO SHARAD subsurface water-ice radar, and THEMIS/USGS imagery), the app scores terrain stability, water-ice access, and solar yield across six real NASA candidate landing sites.

Key features include an Auto-Scan Top 3 Sites engine that evaluates 36 grid coordinates in milliseconds, a Dust Storm Simulator (Tau τ slider) that predicts solar power blackouts, and an ISRU Calculator for daily water and oxygen production. Engineered as a fast, zero-backend edge app (< 100 KB) for low-power hardware, ARES-LOCATE scales seamlessly to ingest live rover LiDAR and orbital telemetry for real human Mars missions.
